title: Your realtime AI is ngmi — Sean DuBois (OpenAI), Kwindla Kramer (Daily)
talk_summary: A WebRTC/voice-AI talk arguing that real-time audio needs WebRTC (UDP, best-effort, jitter buffering) rather than WebSockets (TCP, in-order delivery) to hit sub-second voice-to-voice latency, plus a demo of a Raspberry Pi voice agent on Pipecat. It is almost entirely about edge-to-cloud media transport and voice UX, not about agent orchestration, model routing, review, or CI.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that for latency-critical streams you should drop stale packets rather than block on in-order TCP delivery, because retransmits of old data are worthless inside a tight latency budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's all that machinery that sends packets as fast as possible, ignores packets that don't arrive inside that very tight latency budget
takeaways.numbers: voice-to-voice target ~500ms natural, >1s dooms completion rates; ~10-15% of connections glitch on TCP/WebSockets

takeaways.what_they_do: They note WebRTC gives standard stats/observability APIs for free, whereas a WebSocket implementation forces you to build resampling, packetization, bandwidth estimation, and stats yourself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you also get standard APIs for getting the stats and observability. This is all just built into WebRTC
